overall: The AG found the Planning Board violated the Open Meeting Law when a quorum deliberated while attending the Select Board's June 9 meeting without posted notice, but not intentionally, and found no other improper deliberation.

allegations.summary: A quorum of the Planning Board allegedly deliberated while attending the Select Board's June 9 meeting without the Planning Board having posted notice.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Planning Board deliberated while attending the Select Board’s June 9 meeting, in violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant urged a finding that the quorum's deliberation at the June 9 meeting was an intentional violation of the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: These assertions are insufficient to support a finding of an intentional violation.

allegations.summary: Two Planning Board members allegedly spoke privately and left the room during the June 9 meeting, possibly constituting further serial or chain deliberation outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Where the complainant has offered no evidence beyond mere speculation and conjecture, we do not find a violation with respect to this allegation.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
Caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the Law
remedy_passage: We order the Planning Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
